name: ptswflt
status: OPEN / witness-modeled: the vector and fault-class fixes are closed and pinned per-oracle, but the partial-state phase behavior is NOT differentially closed -- the RTL phase order is an implementation choice (docs/tsw-phase-model.md), graded by witness only until a reorder to the pinned QEMU sequence or a P5 hardware oracle supersedes it
gate_form: WITNESS gate (pselnull/piretgp0 pattern): QEMU's switch_tss_ra orders the phases DIFFERENTLY from the RTL phase model (docs/tsw-phase-model.md), so no whole-trace differential is possible. The golden pins QEMU's honest flow (step-5f asserts on the final record); the RTL side is graded by the step-7w final-GPR witnesses + +ven_faultlog vectors/counts. What the phase order may NOT change -- vector, error code, and attribution per failure class -- IS uniform and is pinned case-by-case in both oracles.
finding: task-switch phase fault injection: the partial-switch state at every phase boundary of docs/tsw-phase-model.md, with the fault semantics (vector/error/CR2) pinned against the pinned emulator's tss_load_seg / switch_tss_ra order

case_map.P1_S_TSW_SAVE: outgoing TSS image page (0x7000) READ-ONLY, ljmp to TSS_I1. QEMU's outgoing ENDPOINT PROBE (switch_tss_ra writes tr.base+0 and tr.base+limit_max before any register save) faults first at tr.base+0; the RTL's first save dword (EIP @ tr.base+0x20) faults at tr.base+0x20. SHARED: #PF err 0x003 (P=1,W=1), CR2 PAGE 0x7000, ZERO save dwords landed (verified by reading the RO page), busy bytes untouched, outgoing context (esp-at-fault == pre-switch ESP). DIFFERS: CR2 low bits (0x7000 vs 0x7020) -- folded as CR2 page only
case_map.P2_S_TSW_READ: incoming TSS image page (0xA000) NOT PRESENT, ljmp to TSS_I2. QEMU faults at the incoming CR3-slot read (tss_base+0x1C, BEFORE any outgoing effect; outgoing EIP slot stays 0). The RTL's phase-1 save COMPLETES (outgoing EIP slot == p2_fire), then its phase-2 read faults at the same +0x1C offset. SHARED: #PF err 0x000 (P=0,W=0), CR2 == 0x0000A01C (BOTH read the incoming image CR3-first -- verified in both sources), busy untouched, outgoing context. DIFFERS: the outgoing save stands in the RTL only (save-stands flag)
case_map.P3_S_TSW_LDT: incoming LDTR = 0x0040 names a NOT-PRESENT LDT descriptor -> #TS(0x0040). QEMU raises it AFTER the whole commit (pselnull oracle gap 1: outgoing busy cleared 0x89, incoming set 0x8B, TR=TSS_I3, CR0.TS=1, delivery in the committed context, espok=0); the RTL raises it in phase 3 with NOTHING moved (espok=1, busy untouched, TR=TSS_RUN)
case_map.P4_S_TSW_SEG: incoming DS = 0x0048 names a SYSTEM (S=0) descriptor (an LDT descriptor used illegally) -> #TS(0x0048) in BOTH oracles (QEMU tss_load_seg's S check). Same post/pre-commit split as P3
case_map.P4b_S_TSW_SEG_CS_np: incoming CS = 0x0050 names a NOT-PRESENT but otherwise well-formed code descriptor (S=1, execute/read, DPL0 == RPL0, in-limit EIP) -> #NP(0x0050) in BOTH oracles: the type/privilege checks precede presence (tss_load_seg; RTL tsw_seg_ts before tsw_seg_np), so a presence-only failure is #NP, not #TS. The phase order still splits the context: RTL pre-commit (espok=1, busy untouched, TR=TSS_RUN), QEMU post-commit (espok=0, busy toggled, TR=TSS_I7)
case_map.P4c_S_TSW_SEG_SS_np: incoming SS = 0x0058 names a NOT-PRESENT but otherwise well-formed data descriptor (S=1, data RW, DPL0 == CPL0) -> #NP(0x0058) in BOTH oracles (CS loads first and is valid). Same post/pre-commit split as P4b
case_map.P4d_S_TSW_SEG_DS_np: incoming DS = 0x0060 names a NOT-PRESENT but otherwise well-formed data descriptor -> #NP(0x0060) in BOTH oracles (CS/SS/ES load, DS faults). Same post/pre-commit split as P4b
case_map.P4e_type_precedes_presence_control: combined-invalid control: incoming CS = 0x0068 names a NOT-PRESENT *data* descriptor -- BOTH a type violation and a presence failure. The type check precedes presence in both oracles, so this is #TS(0x0068), never #NP. Same post/pre-commit split as P4b
case_map.P5a_S_TSW_BUSY_on_write: incoming TSS descriptor on a READ-ONLY GDT page (0x5008). QEMU (clear outgoing busy at step 3, save, then set incoming busy) faults at the busy-SET store (a DWORD at desc+4): TSS_RUN CLEARED (0x89), TSS_I5 still 0x89, save done, TR=TSS_RUN, outgoing context, err 0x003, CR2=0x500C. The RTL faults at phase-5 beat 0 with TSS_RUN BUSY (0x8B); its busy byte write address is desc+5 (CR2=0x500D -- low bits differ, memory-only)
case_map.P5b_between_busy_writes: outgoing TSS_RUN2 descriptor on a READ-ONLY GDT page (0x6008), incoming TSS_I6 on a writable one (0x5010). QEMU faults at its EARLY busy-CLEAR store (before the save): nothing moved, TSS_RUN2 stays 0x8B (the clear failed), TSS_I6 0x89. The RTL saves, validates, SETS the incoming busy bit (0x8B), then faults at the outgoing clear: TSS_RUN2 stays 0x8B (NEVER a running task marked available -- the busy-order safety property) and TSS_I6 is busy-but-not-entered (the recoverable state). The interval between the two busy writes is reachable in the RTL FSM by paging the two TSS descriptors onto different GDT pages; QEMU has no analogous interval (its busy-clear is before the save, its busy-set after it)
case_map.P5c_CALL_backlink: lcall to TSS_I11 (a NESTING switch): the CALL form writes the outgoing TR selector into the incoming TSS back-link word at offset 0, and the outgoing descriptor is NOT cleared in either oracle (the caller remains an active task, returned to via NT-IRET). The incoming image page (0x1E000) is READ-ONLY, so the back-link store faults: #PF err 0x003, CR2 = 0x0001E000 in BOTH oracles, pre-commit in BOTH (TR=TSS_RUN2, the outgoing task since the P5b prep's LTR; EFLAGS.NT never set). ORDER DELTA, honestly enumerated: QEMU's switch_tss_ra writes the back-link BEFORE its incoming busy-set (seg_helper.c: the SWITCH_TSS_CALL cpu_stw at tss_base+0 precedes tss_set_busy(...,1)), so TSS_I11 stays 0x89; this core's S_TSW_BUSY sets the incoming busy bit at beat 0 and writes the back-link at beat 1 (core_bus_driver.svh), so TSS_I11 is busy-but-not-entered (0x8B) -- the recoverable state

witnesses.exit_edi: (P1 cr2 & ~0xFFF) | P1 err = 0x00007003 -- IDENTICAL in both oracles
witnesses.exit_ebp: P3<<16 | P4, a case half-word = (espok<<15)|(vector<<8)|errcode: RTL 0x8A408A48 / QEMU golden 0x0A400A48
witnesses.exit_ebx: P4b<<16 | P4c: RTL 0x8B508B58 / QEMU golden 0x0B500B58 (both oracles #NP; espok splits)
witnesses.exit_ecx: P4d<<16 | P4e: RTL 0x8B608A68 / QEMU golden 0x0B600A68 (#NP(0x60) then the type-first #TS(0x68) control)
witnesses.exit_edx: (busy6<<26) | 0x0E300F4; busy6 = the six P5 busy bytes' BUSY bit (acc == 0x8B) as p5a_run,p5a_inc,p5b_inc,p5b_run,p5c_inc,p5c_run: RTL 0xBCE300F4 / QEMU golden 0x14E300F4. p5a_inc is clear in BOTH (its busy-set write is the one that faults); p5b_run and p5c_run are busy in BOTH (the outgoing descriptor NEVER becomes available mid-switch)
witnesses.exit_eax: (P5c cr2 >> 4 << 8) | 0x42 = 0x001E0042 -- IDENTICAL in both oracles (the back-link store faults at incoming TSS offset 0; 0x42 is the isa-debug-exit code)
witnesses.slots_0x2800: per-case 20-byte slots (+0 vec, +4 err, +8 esp-at-fault, +12 cr2, +16 saved_eip): P1 err=0x003 cr2 page 0x7000 saved_eip=p1 ljmp; P2 err=0x000 cr2=0xA01C; P3 vec=10 err=0x0040 saved_eip=the ljmp (BOTH oracles -- QEMU's raise restores the PC to the ljmp even though the switch committed); P4 vec=10 err=0x0048; P4b vec=11 err=0x0050; P4c vec=11 err=0x0058; P4d vec=11 err=0x0060; P4e vec=10 err=0x0068; P5a vec=14 err=0x003; P5b vec=14 err=0x003; P5c vec=14 err=0x003 cr2=0x1E000
witnesses.0x2004: P1 outgoing EIP slot == 0 (BOTH oracles land zero dwords; the RO page is readable so this is verified, not assumed)
witnesses.0x201c: P3 TR after the fault: RTL 0x0018 (TSS_RUN) / QEMU 0x0030 (TSS_I3, committed)
witnesses.0x202c: P4 TR after the fault: RTL 0x0018 / QEMU 0x0038
witnesses.0x2038: P5a raw CR2: QEMU 0x0000500C (busy DWORD store at desc+4) / RTL 0x0000500D (busy byte at desc+5)
witnesses.0x2050_0x205c: P4b/P4c/P4d/P4e espok flags: RTL 1/1/1/1 (pre-commit) / QEMU 0/0/0/0 (post-commit) -- folded into the ebx/ecx exit halves
witnesses.0x2060_0x2068: P5c: TSS_RUN2 acc 0x8B BOTH (CALL never clears the caller), TSS_I11 acc RTL 0x8B / QEMU 0x89 (the busy-set/back-link order delta), CR2 0x0001E000 BOTH

oracle_notes.phase_order: QEMU switch_tss_ra (verified in the pinned source): (1) read ALL incoming TSS state, (2) probe outgoing TSS endpoints, (3) clear outgoing busy for JMP/IRET (NOT for CALL), (4) save outgoing state, (5) CALL back-link word at tss_base+0, (6) set incoming busy, (7) commit TR/CR0.TS/CR3/EIP/GPRs (selectors only, hidden caches ZEROED), (8) validate incoming LDTR, (9) tss_load_seg per segment (CS,SS,ES,DS,FS,GS), (10) CS EIP-vs-limit check. The RTL (docs/tsw-phase-model.md): (0/0b) source+TR validation, (1) S_TSW_SAVE, (2) S_TSW_READ, (3) S_TSW_LDT, (4) S_TSW_SEG, (5) S_TSW_BUSY (beat 0 incoming busy-set; beat 1 back-link for CALL / outgoing clear for JMP; commit last). EVERY injection lands in a different partial state in the two oracles, hence the witness-gate form
oracle_notes.fault_semantics_uniform: the phase ORDER is free to differ (and does); the fault SEMANTICS are not. tss_load_seg ranks S/type/privilege/null/bounds failures as #TS(selector & 0xfffc) BEFORE the presence check, a presence-ONLY failure as #NP(selector & 0xfffc), and the CS EIP-vs-limit check AFTER presence. S_TSW_SEG now ranks identically (tsw_seg_ts / tsw_seg_np in core_tsw.svh, the EIP limit folded into tsw_seg_ts only when the descriptor is present). P4b/P4c/P4d pin the #NP branch, P4e pins that type still precedes presence (#TS), P4 pins the S=0 #TS branch -- every vector + error code is uniform across the two oracles
oracle_notes.np_vs_ts_split_RETIRED: RETIRED 2026-08-05. The original manifest recorded a vector split: a NOT-PRESENT incoming task segment was #NP(sel) in QEMU but #TS(sel) in the RTL (the blanket tsw_seg_bad covered P=0 alongside type/privilege), and P4 used an S=0 descriptor to keep the vector uniform. The RTL's S_TSW_SEG fault select now ranks exactly like the pinned tss_load_seg (presence-ONLY -> start_fault(8'd11), everything else -> start_fault(8'd10)), so P4b/P4c/P4d were added as uniform-vector #NP cases and P4e as the type-precedes-presence control. A scratch build with the select reverted to unconditional start_fault(8'd10) witnesses #TS where #NP is required -- the negative control in validation.negative_control
oracle_notes.post_commit_artifact: QEMU's post-commit faults (P3/P4/P4b/P4c/P4d/P4e) are delivered through the JUST-committed SS hidden cache, which at that point is only SELECTOR-loaded (base=0, limit=0, FLAGS=0) -- tss_load_seg has not run. get_sp_mask(flags=0) = 0xFFFF, so the exception frame is pushed at (esp & 0xFFFF) with ESP[31:16] preserved, NOT at esp, and the IRET pops it from the masked address (QEMU's own comment: 'from this point, any exception which occurs can give problems'). QEMU ALSO restores env->eip to the transfer instruction via raise_exception_err_ra's cpu_restore_state, so the saved EIP is the ljmp in BOTH oracles. The shared fcommon handler locates the frame by a scratch-push probe (below every candidate frame), reads err/saved_eip from the located frame, writes the resume EIP there, and scrubs both candidate dwords so a later case cannot see the leftover
oracle_notes.qemu_cr2s: P1: 0x00007000 (probe store at tr.base+0); P2: 0x0000A01C (incoming CR3-slot read); P5a: 0x0000500C (tss_set_busy's DWORD store at desc+4); P5b: 0x0000600C; P5c: 0x0001E000 (the CALL back-link WORD store at tss_base+0)
oracle_notes.invlpg: PTE changes are INVLPG'd after every toggle (the psamepf TLB lesson)

blocking_rtl_defect: RESOLVED 2026-08-04 (historical, first six-case version). The first RTL run took NO fault for P1 (the RO outgoing-save write) and the switch completed -- S_TSW_SAVE and S_TSW_BUSY never set cur_is_w, so the write-permission check never ran on their beats (WP-on RO writes sailed through). Fixed by marking both states' cur_is_w_nat (rtl/core/core.sv); every injected fault then fired with the documented partial states

residuals.call_source_backlink: CLOSED 2026-08-05 by P5c (see case_map): the CALL-source back-link write is fault-injected on a read-only incoming image page; the QEMU-vs-RTL phase-5 order delta (back-link before busy-set vs beat-0 busy-set) is enumerated there and graded through the p5c_inc busy byte
residuals.controls: intentionally omitted -- ptask/ptaskcpl/ptaskpg/pcalltss pin the clean JMP/CALL/NT-IRET switches differentially

description: WITNESS gate for task-switch phase fault injection. Eleven CPL0 injections, one per phase boundary of docs/tsw-phase-model.md plus the incoming-segment fault-class matrix: P1 outgoing-save page read-only (S_TSW_SAVE), P2 incoming-read page not-present (S_TSW_READ), P3 incoming LDTR not-present (S_TSW_LDT, #TS(0x40)), P4 incoming DS is a system descriptor (S_TSW_SEG, #TS(0x48)), P4b/P4c/P4d incoming CS/SS/DS not-present but otherwise well-formed (S_TSW_SEG, #NP(0x50)/#NP(0x58)/#NP(0x60) in BOTH oracles -- presence-only failure, uniform vector), P4e not-present DATA as incoming CS (the type check precedes presence: #TS(0x68) control), P5a incoming busy-byte write on a read-only GDT page (S_TSW_BUSY), P5b outgoing busy-byte write read-only with the incoming writable (between the two busy writes -- the safe state: outgoing NEVER available mid-switch), P5c CALL-source back-link store on a read-only incoming image page (#PF, CR2 = incoming TSS offset 0, outgoing busy never cleared). QEMU's switch_tss_ra orders the phases differently on every axis (incoming read first, busy-clear before save, post-commit LDTR/segment validation, back-link before busy-set), so the test is a witness gate: the golden pins QEMU's honest flow including the post-commit delivery artifact (the frame pushed through the selector-only SS cache at esp&0xFFFF, located by the scratch-push probe in fcommon), and the RTL is graded by final-GPR witnesses + +ven_faultlog. Each case records old/new TR, both busy bytes, outgoing image dwords, CR2, error code, ESP-at-fault, and the saved fault EIP into slots; seven packed words leave in edi/esi/ebp/ebx/ecx/edx/eax.
